title: High-precision ab initio calculations of nuclear binding energies: Tin isotopes from dripline to dripline
authors: Urban Vernik, Pepijn Demol, Thomas Duguet, Alexander Tichai
abstract: The location of the neutron drip line in tin isotopes has important consequences for our fundamental understanding of nuclear structure and nuclear forces as well as for astrophysical nucleosynthesis. Performing high-precision ab initio calculations of even-even tin isotopes from $N=50$ to $N=126$ based on chiral two- and three-nucleon interactions, the predicted drip-line location is found to be highly sensitive to the employed nuclear interactions and to exhibit tension with recent energy-density-functional predictions. On the neutron-deficient side, results are consistent with extrapolated two-neutron separation energies constrained by recent Penning-trap mass measurements.
summary: This paper calculates the binding energies of tin isotopes near the neutron drip line using advanced *ab initio* methods based on chiral Effective Field Theory. By employing the BCCSD[T] approximation, the authors achieve high precision and map out trends in nuclear structure, highlighting discrepancies between theoretical models and experimental constraints.
main_problem: To perform high-precision calculations of nuclear binding energies for tin isotopes across the neutron drip line.
main_result: The BCCSD[T] approach significantly reduces many-body uncertainty, showing sensitivity in predicting the drip-line location compared to Energy Density Functional models.
method: Bogoliubov Coupled-Cluster (BCC) theory, extended to include leading triples corrections (BCCSD[T]), is used to solve the many-body Schrödinger equation.
model_or_system: The study focuses on even-even Tin isotopes ($	ext{Sn}$) ranging from $N=50$ towards the neutron dripline. Calculations utilize chiral Effective Field Theory ($\chi	ext{EFT}$) two- and three-nucleon interactions within the BCC framework.
key_observables: Binding energies ($E_0$) and two-neutron separation energies ($S_{2n}$).
important_parameters: The calculation uses a one-body spherical harmonic oscillator basis ($\hbar\omega = 12 	ext{ MeV}$) and incorporates interactions up to the three-nucleon level.
main_assumptions: Approximations are made in solving the cluster amplitudes, notably using the non-iterative BCCSD[T] method, which introduces systematic uncertainties.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares ground-state energies ($E_0$) for $	ext{Sn}$ isotopes using BCCSD and BCCSD[T] against VS-IMSRG results. Figure 2 shows $S_{2n}$ around the $N=50$ shell closure.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework (BCC theory, Hamiltonian formulation), presents the systematic improvement achieved by including triples corrections (BCCSD[T]), and compares resulting binding energies and separation energies across the isotopic chain to experimental data and other advanced calculations.
why_interesting: While focused on nuclear physics, the rigorous application of many-body perturbation theory techniques like Coupled Cluster methods for calculating ground state properties is a highly sophisticated theoretical tool relevant to strongly correlated quantum systems in general.
